validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed independent of GEM/gem.wiki. Kinder Morgan's own operations page (kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index) describes 'The Wyoming Interstate pipeline (WIC)' as an active interstate system offering Firm and Interruptible Transportation Service. Rextag (rextag.com/pages/wyoming-interstate), an independent pipeline-data reseller pulling FERC-mandated informational postings, separately confirms WIC, gives 'Operating at more than 50% capacity' (explicit operating-status language), Owner Kinder Morgan Inc., Operator Wyoming Interstate Company LLC. Four separate FERC dockets on govinfo.gov corroborate the entity is real and active in different years: CP05-54-000 (2005 Piceance Basin Expansion, Notice of Application, govinfo FR-2005-02-09/E5-526), CP19-206-000 (2019 Medicine Bow Lateral abandonment-by-sale notice), and CP23-59-000 (2023 CIG/WIC joint application re: Powder River Lateral MAOP reduction) -- three different subjects/years, none GEM-derived. NGI trade press (naturalgasintel.com, 2005 article on the CP05-54 certificate) independently reports the same expansion with matching figures (142 mi/24-in/$120M/341 MMcf/d), corroborating the FERC record. CLASSIFICATION: correct as recorded. WIC is FERC-certificated under NGA section 7(c) (govinfo E5-526 explicitly: 'application... for an order granting a certificate of public convenience... to construct and operate') and sells Firm/Interruptible Transportation Service -- the definition of a transmission pipeline, not gathering/distribution. Fuel=Gas is correct (all sources describe it as a natural-gas transportation system). DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's 'Kinder Morgan Rockies trio' (P0168 CIG, P0270 TransColorado). WIC, CIG and TransColorado are three genuinely separate FERC-certificated systems, not the same pipe under different names -- KM's own site and the 2023 joint CIG/WIC filing describe them as affiliated-but-distinct entities with their own capacity-lease arrangements between them (a 'CIG/WIC Capacity Lease Agreement' on Line No. 72A and the Laramie Jumper Compressor, per CP23-59-000) rather than one system double-counted. No duplicate concern. Of the row's 2 harvested gem.wiki citations, both were opened: the bit.ly/2sYXPRn link resolves (curl -L) to abarrelfull.wikidot.com -- BANNED, unusable, and its content was not used for anything; the offshore-technology.com link returned 403 to a browser-UA curl and a Wayback lookup (archive.org/wayback/available) was rate-limited (429) for the whole session at every retry attempted -- left unread, not confirmed dead, no value depends on it.

validity.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown from 800 mi toward ~850 mi (the figure every independent description of the WIC system states), or confirm the sheet is deliberately scoping to mainline-only mileage excluding laterals -- currently undocumented either way.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM has LengthKnown=800.00 mi for the whole WIC system row. Three separately published descriptions of the system all state ~850 miles instead: Kinder Morgan's own operations page ('The Wyoming Interstate pipeline (WIC) consists of approximately 850 miles of pipeline'), Rextag ('Miles of Pipeline: 850'), and PipeRiv ('With approximately 850 miles of pipeline, WIC is comprised of a mainline system... and several lateral pipeline systems'). Flagging honestly: all three likely trace back to the same underlying company-description language used in WIC's FERC-mandated informational postings, so this is closer to one strong, consistently-repeated origin than three fully independent measurements -- but it is nonetheless a real, material, and unanimous conflict with the sheet's 800. PipeRiv's phrasing also clarifies '850 miles' is the MAINLINE PLUS LATERALS total, which raises a real possibility GEM's 800 is trying to record mainline-only mileage on a different (undocumented) basis -- I could not find a source that isolates mainline-only miles, so I am not proposing 800 be treated as simply wrong, only that it disagrees with every public description of the full system and needs a human decision on scope before the cell is touched.

validity.recommendation: Verify Capacity before trusting either number -- Rextag's 2,300 MMcf/d is a single source and should not simply replace the sheet's 3,900 MMcf/d without a second, stronger source (FERC order, EIA, or an operator tariff/rate case filing stating the certificated capacity).
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Capacity=3900.00 MMcf/d. The only capacity figure I could locate anywhere for the WIC SYSTEM (not an individual expansion increment) is Rextag's 'System Capacity: 2.3 Bcf/d' (2,300 MMcf/d) -- a 41% gap from the sheet, too large to be rounding or unit confusion. I could not find a second source stating either number for the whole system: EIA's pipeline pages returned 403/406 to every UA and Accept-header combination I tried (their .xlsx endpoint also 406'd); FERC eLibrary's search UI is a JS SPA I could not query via curl; multiple targeted Brave-engine searches for '3,900 MMcf/d' or '2,300 MMcf/d' + Wyoming Interstate returned nothing. The FERC dockets I did read state only INCREMENTAL added capacity for specific expansions (341 MMcf/d for the 2005 Piceance Basin Expansion, CP05-54; a further 180 MMcf/d westbound addition targeted for 2025 per an East Daley Capital trade note on the Wamsutter compressor project) -- neither of those is a system total and neither confirms or refutes the sheet's 3,900. Because I have only one weak data point and no way to adjudicate it against the sheet, I am leaving the fills[] entry for this unit UNRESOLVED rather than forcing either number, and flagging this validity concern so a human knows the current 3,900 is uncorroborated, not confirmed.

Per gem_schema.md's FuelSource gotcha, this column wants a named upstream FIELD/PLANT/FACILITY, not a basin and not 'Natural Gas'. The best lead I found -- Kinder Morgan's own WIC company overview (via piperiv.com's quote of it) -- says WIC 'provid[es] takeaway capacity from the Overthrust, Piceance, Uinta, Powder River and Green River basins,' which names BASINS, not specific fields or plants. I have deliberately not forced this into the value field (the Saudi-gas sweep's 'Natural Gas' mis-fill is exactly the failure mode this schema note warns against), and am leaving it UNRESOLVED with the basin names recorded here as a lead: a human or a follow-up pass could narrow this to a specific receipt-point field/plant along WIC's mainline if the schema's convention for a multi-basin US system accepts basin-level entries.
